subject: geography
title: Weather & Climate Adventure: Extreme Weather
welcome_lead: Beast from the East, Storm Desmond, summer heatwaves — is UK weather getting more extreme?
meta_desc: GCSE Geography extreme weather — UK case studies, climate change, evidence.
final_note: You explored UK extreme weather case studies and the evidence for climate change.

concepts.def: Weather very different from the average
Prolonged period of unusually hot weather
Long-term shift in global climate patterns
Heat trapped by gases in the atmosphere
Action to reduce causes of climate change

walkthroughs.body_html:
Storm Desmond (Dec 2015): record rainfall in Cumbria, severe flooding in Carlisle.

Beast from the East (Feb 2018): Polar continental air brought heavy snow, ~17 deaths.

Heatwave July 2022: UK hit 40.3°C at Coningsby — first ever 40°C reading.

Global temperatures have risen ~1.1°C since 1880.

Evidence: shrinking Arctic sea ice, retreating glaciers, rising sea levels (~20cm since 1900), earlier spring blossoms, ice cores showing rising CO2.

Causes: burning fossil fuels, deforestation, agriculture (methane) — all increase greenhouse gases.

Mitigation: renewables, carbon capture, reforestation, international agreements (Paris 2015).

Adaptation: flood defences, drought-resistant crops, changing building design.

mcqs.q: What did the UK record for the first time during the July 2022 heatwave?
Which is an example of climate change MITIGATION (not adaptation)?

numericals.q: Approximately how much have global average temperatures risen since 1880 (degrees C)?
numericals.hint: Just over 1 degree — but huge impact.
